name: The Null Brief
description: A thirty-minute weekly pirate news broadcast distributed via encrypted mesh nodes across the Shelf and lower Tier 2 zones, hosted by the anonymous collective known only as the Null Desk — identities obscured by signal-lag voice modulation and rotating visual avatars. Each episode focuses on a single verified corporate crime: a specific contract, a specific death, a specific ledger discrepancy, supported by leaked documents displayed on-screen with source-protection redactions. The broadcast has been formally condemned by four corponations and informally praised by two others who benefit from its reporting on rivals.
cultural_impact: Established the 'single-story discipline' format — one verifiable crime per episode, no editorializing — as the gold standard for underground journalism, explicitly in reaction to the sensationalism of earlier pirate broadcasts.
story_hooks: A player character receives a dead-drop containing next week's Null Brief episode, already produced — but the crime it describes hasn't happened yet.
One of the Null Desk collective has been compromised and is feeding the corponation sanitized versions of stories before broadcast, and the others don't know.
A corponation security team has been using the Null Brief's own verification methods to identify and eliminate its sources, and the collective needs outside help to find the leak.
